tasks.title: Read and aggregate the JSONL records into one deterministic data object

details.contract:
Create `src/shared/telemetry/html.ts`. It imports `./report` for `type ReportData` only and nothing else; it performs no IO.

export function escapeHtml(value: string): string;
export function renderHtml(data: ReportData, meta: { readonly generated_at: string; readonly since: string | null }): string;

The output is one HTML document built by one template literal: a `<style>` block with all CSS inline, the panels below, then a single `<script>` block with inline JS (no framework, no import, no fetch) that draws the per-day unresolved-ratio bars from the embedded blob. The data is embedded once as `JSON.stringify(data)` with every `<` replaced by `\\u003c` so a `</script>` inside any string cannot close the tag; every other interpolated string goes through `escapeHtml` (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`).

Panels, in this order: header (window: `since` or `all records`, `generated_at`, totals: records, calls, index runs, sessions, unparsed lines, install ids, days); per-tool table (tool, calls, status mix, error-code mix, p50/p95/mean/max `duration_ms`, truncation count, mean `budget_used_ratio`, eq/gte counts); truncation (count, rate, reasons); relations (`eq` count, `gte` count, `eq` ratio); coverage (stale calls, mean `unresolved_edges`); argument names (name, calls) with a one-line note that names only, never values, are recorded; the unresolved-ratio trend as one bar per day plus its numeric value; the index-run table (ts, mode, exit code, duration, files seen/indexed/skipped/failed/changed, unresolved ratio, db bytes, generation advanced); sessions (by mode, by root kind, by size bucket); and an empty-state panel that replaces every table body when `data.totals.records === 0`.

Hard constraints: no `http://`, no `https://`, no `src=`, no `<link`, no `@import`, no `url(` anywhere in the output — the file must render with the network off. No integer is rendered without its label, no absolute path is rendered, and `install_id`/`session_id` values are never printed (only their counts). Formatting goes through two small local helpers (`fmtInt` with `toLocaleString("en-US")` replaced by a fixed grouping so output stays byte-stable, and `fmtRatio` with 2 decimals) — do not call `Date` or `Math.random`.

Determinism is a hard requirement: `renderHtml(data, meta)` called twice with the same arguments must be byte-identical.
details.goal: One pure renderer turns the aggregated data into a single self-contained HTML file with inline CSS, inline JS and an embedded data blob, with every interpolated string escaped.
steps: Declare `escapeHtml` and `renderHtml` with the signatures above.
Write the document skeleton: doctype, `<style>` block, header panel, and one container per panel.
Render the per-tool table, truncation, relations, coverage and argument-name panels from `data`.
Render the trend bars, the index-run table and the session panels; add the empty-state branch for zero records.
Add the inline `<script>` that draws the trend bars from the embedded `\\u003c`-escaped JSON blob.
Check the rendered output manually for the forbidden substrings and confirm two renders are byte-identical.

tasks.title: Render one self-contained HTML report with inline CSS, JS and data

details.contract:
Create `src/shared/telemetry/cli.ts`. It imports `#shared/config` (`loadConfig`, `flagValue`), `./report` (`aggregate`, `isSinceLiteral`, `parseSince`, `readRecords`), `./html` (`renderHtml`) and `node:fs`/`node:path`. It never imports `src/index`, a tool or the indexer, and never needs a graph.

export async function runTelemetry(argv: readonly string[]): Promise<number>;

Semantics, all of which the doc and the tests repeat verbatim:
- `argv` is the arguments after the `telemetry` token; `loadConfig({ argv })` resolves `repoRoot`, `dataDir` and `telemetry.dir` from `--repo-root`/`--data-dir` exactly like every other mode.
- `--out <path>`: default `join(config.telemetry.dir, "report.html")`; a relative value resolves against `repoRoot` (the same rule as `--data-dir`); an existing file is overwritten; parent directories are created with `mkdirSync(dirname(out), { recursive: true })`.
- `--since <YYYY-MM-DD | Nd>`: default = all records. A value that is neither shape is a usage error: the reason and the usage line go to stderr and the function returns 2 **without writing a file**. `--help`/`-h` prints the usage to stdout and returns 0 without writing a file.
- Zero records is not an error: the report is still written (with its empty-state panel) and the exit code is 0.
- A corrupt or partial line is skipped and counted, never fatal: the count reaches the report through `aggregate`'s `unparsed` and the stdout line.
- Success writes exactly one stdout line: `wrote <absolute path> (<n> records, <m> unparsed lines)` followed by a newline, and returns 0. A write failure writes the message to stderr and returns 1.
- The generated HTML never contains the output path or the data dir; only the stdout line names them.
- `runTelemetry` is async for symmetry with `main` but performs only synchronous IO; it must not call `process.exit`.

`meta.generated_at` for the render is `new Date().toISOString()` computed once, in this module — the renderer itself takes no clock, which is what keeps it byte-stable under test.
details.goal: One function implements the verb: it resolves the config from the flags, reads the records, aggregates and renders them, writes exactly one file, prints one line, and maps every failure to the project's exit codes.
steps: Declare `runTelemetry` and a local `usage` string naming the verb and its two flags.
Handle `--help`/`-h`, then read and validate `--out` and `--since` (missing value or malformed `--since` -> stderr + usage + return 2).
Resolve the output path (default `<telemetry.dir>/report.html`, relative against `repoRoot`), then `loadConfig` and `readRecords`.
Aggregate, render with a single `generated_at`, `mkdirSync` and `writeFileSync`; on a write error write the reason to stderr and return 1.
Write the one stdout line and return 0.
Run typecheck and lint.

details.contract:
Two existing files, additive changes only.

`tests/cli.test.ts` (spawns the real command, `cleanEnv()` already deletes every `SANGKAR_*` key): add three cases.
1. `sangkar telemetry` in a fixture data dir that already holds one hand-written `telemetry/<date>.jsonl` with one `call` record: exit 0, stdout is exactly one line matching `/^wrote .*report\.html \(1 records, 0 unparsed lines\)$/`, `<dataDir>/telemetry/report.html` exists and is non-empty, and stderr carries no error line.
